_comment: Shared CGST Rule 46(b) invoice-number cases. Read by
(lib/invoices/gst.validateInvoiceNo) are exercised on the SAME numbers.
The browser copy exists for keystroke feedback and nothing else — the
server refuses independently, at create, at edit and at issue. It is a
mirror in the same sense apps/web/lib/gst/gstin.ts is, and it is pinned the
same way: adding a case here adds it to both suites, and changing one
implementation without the other fails here.
'legal' is the whole answer. The two implementations word their refusals
differently on purpose — the server names the character it found, the
browser tells a CA mid-keystroke what is allowed — so the message is NOT

Both implementations TRIM before judging, and the Pydantic field validator returns the trimmed value, so a padded number is legal AND is stored clean. That is why '  INV-0001  ' is in the legal list rather than the illegal one.

illegal.why: '#' is not in the permitted set
underscore is not in the permitted set
a space is not in the permitted set
a full stop is not in the permitted set
a backslash is not the permitted slash
a rupee glyph is not in the permitted set
